title: Undeciphered: Linear A of Minoan Crete
summary: Since its rediscovery in 1900, no Linear A text has been deciphered. Sound values borrowed from its deciphered offspring, Linear B, can be pronounced but do not yield an understood language.
why: It records the Minoans in their own words, beside a related script, Linear B, that we can read.
question: What language did the Minoans write in Linear A?
evidence: About 1,400 inscriptions (about 7,400 sign tokens), roughly half from Hagia Triada; many signs match Linear B, giving approximate but uncertain sound values.
wouldSettle: A bilingual inscription or a much larger corpus of readable Linear A texts.
